name: Enable Game Mode
description: Windows Game Mode on for better game scheduling.

name: Disable Xbox Game DVR
description: Stops background recording (real FPS drain).
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\System\GameConfigStore" /v GameDVR_Enabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f & reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\GameDVR" /v AllowGameDVR /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKCU\System\GameConfigStore" /v GameDVR_Enabled /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f & reg delete "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\GameDVR" /v AllowGameDVR /f

name: Disable Game Bar Capture
description: Turns off Win+G background capture.

name: Disable Fullscreen Optimizations
description: Global FSO off for lower input lag (test per game).
detailedDescription: Fullscreen Optimizations is Windows running a borderless window that pretends to be exclusive fullscreen, which lets the compositor add its own frame of latency. Turning it off globally hands the display back to the game. Undo it if a game starts flickering on alt-tab or loses HDR.
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\System\GameConfigStore" /v GameDVR_FSEBehaviorMode /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f & reg add "HKCU\System\GameConfigStore" /v GameDVR_HonorUserFSEBehaviorMode /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
originalRevert: reg delete "HKCU\System\GameConfigStore" /v GameDVR_FSEBehaviorMode /f & reg delete "HKCU\System\GameConfigStore" /v GameDVR_HonorUserFSEBehaviorMode /f

name: Disable Mouse Acceleration
description: Raw, consistent aim (turns off pointer precision).
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v MouseSpeed /t REG_SZ /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v MouseThreshold1 /t REG_SZ /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v MouseThreshold2 /t REG_SZ /d 0 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v MouseSpeed /t REG_SZ /d 1 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v MouseThreshold1 /t REG_SZ /d 6 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v MouseThreshold2 /t REG_SZ /d 10 /f

name: Visual Effects: Performance
description: Disables animations/shadows for a snappier desktop.

name: Disable Transparency
description: Turns off transparency effects (tiny GPU/CPU save).

name: Remove Menu Show Delay
description: Menus open instantly instead of after 400ms.

name: Remove Startup Delay
description: Autostart apps launch immediately.

name: Show File Extensions
description: Always show file extensions in Explorer.

name: Disable Fast Startup
description: Cleaner full shutdowns (fixes some driver quirks). Booting takes longer, because Windows starts cold instead of resuming a saved kernel.
detailedDescription: Shutdown normally hibernates the kernel and drivers to disk so the next boot can skip initialising them. That saved state is also why a driver problem survives a shutdown and only a restart clears it. Undo it if you would rather have the faster boot back.

name: Disable Core Isolation (HVCI)
description: RISKY: lowers security (memory integrity). Can raise FPS. Reboot.
detailedDescription: Memory integrity runs the kernel's driver-signing checks inside a hypervisor, which costs a few percent CPU in games. Switching it off removes a real defence against malicious drivers, not a cosmetic one. Leave it on unless you have measured the difference and decided it is worth it.

name: Disable VBS
description: RISKY: disables Virtualization-Based Security. Reboot.
detailedDescription: Virtualisation-based security isolates parts of Windows inside a hypervisor, and everything running above it pays for the indirection. This is the broadest of the security trade-offs here, and on some machines the largest single gain. Undo it if you handle anything you would not want a rootkit near.

name: Hardware GPU Scheduling (HAGS)
description: Reboot required. Can lower latency - test on your rig.
detailedDescription: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling lets the graphics card manage its own work queue instead of the CPU driver thread doing it. Whether that helps depends entirely on your GPU and driver: it can lower latency, and it can raise it. Requires a restart, and undo it if frame times get worse rather than better.

name: Disable MPO
description: Fixes flicker/stutter on some NVIDIA/AMD setups. Driver-dependent: on setups where the overlay was working it can introduce the stutter it fixes elsewhere. Undo it if the picture gets worse.
detailedDescription: Multi-plane overlay lets the display engine compose windows without a full GPU pass, which is efficient and, on some driver versions, the source of flicker and stutter in windowed games. Turning it off makes the GPU do the composition itself. Undo it if you notice higher GPU load at idle or on multi-monitor setups.

name: Increase TdrDelay
description: Fewer 'display driver stopped responding' timeouts. If the GPU really does hang, you now stare at a frozen screen for ten seconds instead of two before Windows resets the driver.
detailedDescription: Timeout Detection and Recovery is the watchdog that resets a graphics driver which has not responded for two seconds. Raising it to ten gives a briefly overloaded GPU time to finish instead of being reset mid-frame. The cost is that a genuine hang now locks the screen five times longer before Windows steps in.

name: Ultimate Performance Plan
description: Creates & activates the Ultimate Performance power plan.
detailedDescription: Creates & activates the Ultimate Performance power plan.

name: Min Processor State 100%
description: Keeps CPU from downclocking (more consistent frames). The CPU never clocks down, so it runs hotter, draws more power at idle and the fans stay louder.
detailedDescription: The power scheme's minimum processor state is the floor below which the CPU will not clock down. Setting it to 100 percent pins every core at its base clock, so nothing has to ramp up when a frame suddenly needs it. Undo it if the machine idles hot or the fans never settle.
originalCommand: powercfg -setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_PROCESSOR PROCTHROTTLEMIN 100 & powercfg -setactive SCHEME_CURRENT
originalRevert: powercfg -setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_PROCESSOR PROCTHROTTLEMIN 5 & powercfg -setactive SCHEME_CURRENT

name: Disable Core Parking
description: Keeps all cores active (core parking, not C-states). Every core stays awake, which costs idle power and heat for a gain most games will not notice.
detailedDescription: Core parking puts idle cores into a deep sleep the scheduler must wake them from, which costs a fraction of a millisecond at exactly the wrong moment. Requiring all cores to stay unparked removes that wake-up. This is core parking, not C-states - the cores still idle, they just stay available.
originalCommand: powercfg -setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_PROCESSOR CPMINCORES 100 & powercfg -setactive SCHEME_CURRENT
originalRevert: powercfg -setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_PROCESSOR CPMINCORES 0 & powercfg -setactive SCHEME_CURRENT

name: Disable Power Throttling
description: Stops Windows throttling the CPU under load. Higher power draw and more heat under load, and on a laptop noticeably less battery.
detailedDescription: Power throttling lets Windows slow down threads it considers background work, and it occasionally misjudges a game's helper threads. Switching it off removes that judgement entirely. On a desktop the cost is watts and heat; on a laptop it is battery, which is why the app withholds it there.

name: Disable USB Selective Suspend
description: No USB standby (mouse/keyboard lag). USB devices are kept powered at all times, which costs a little idle power and battery.
detailedDescription: Selective suspend powers down USB devices that have been idle, and waking a mouse or keyboard from it takes a moment you can feel. Disabling it keeps every port powered. Undo it if you want the idle draw back, or if a device runs warm while unused.

name: Foreground Priority Boost
description: Win32PrioritySeparation = 26 (favors the active app). Background work is starved while a game is in focus: downloads, encodes and compiles slow down.
detailedDescription: Win32PrioritySeparation controls how much longer a foreground thread gets to run before the scheduler moves on. Value 26 gives the active window a distinctly longer slice. The other side of that is background work getting shorter ones, so downloads and encodes slow while a game has focus.

name: System Responsiveness for Games
description: Gives games more CPU headroom (MMCSS = 0). Nothing is held back for background services any more, so heavy load can make recording or voice chat stutter.
detailedDescription: SystemResponsiveness is the share of CPU time the multimedia scheduler reserves for non-multimedia work, twenty percent by default. Setting it to zero reserves nothing, so a game can use everything it asks for. Undo it if recording or voice chat starts breaking up under load.

name: Keep Kernel in RAM
description: DisablePagingExecutive - needs plenty of RAM.
detailedDescription: DisablePagingExecutive keeps kernel code and drivers resident in RAM instead of allowing them to be paged out to disk. With memory to spare that removes a rare but real stall. Below about 16 GB it takes memory from things that need it more, which is why the app checks first.
originalCommand: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v DisablePagingExecutive /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v DisablePagingExecutive /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

name: Disable Dynamic Tick
description: Timer tweak that can smooth frame pacing.
detailedDescription: Timer tweak that can smooth frame pacing.

name: HPET off (useplatformclock)
description: RISKY/TEST: can help or hurt - always benchmark.
detailedDescription: RISKY/TEST: can help or hurt - always benchmark.

name: Disable Spectre/Meltdown Mitigations
description: RISKY: turns off CPU security mitigations for small perf.
detailedDescription: The Spectre and Meltdown mitigations add checks around speculative execution, and those checks cost measurable CPU throughput. Removing them re-exposes your machine to a class of attack that reads memory across process boundaries. This is the one tweak here that trades a documented vulnerability for frames.
originalCommand: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v FeatureSettingsOverride /t REG_DWORD /d 3 /f

name: Disable Background Apps
description: Stops UWP apps running in the background.

name: Disable SysMain (Superfetch)
description: Can reduce disk churn (marginal on SSD).
detailedDescription: SysMain watches which programs you launch and preloads them into spare RAM. On a hard disk that was a large win; on an SSD the disk is fast enough that the prediction rarely pays for its own background reads. Undo it if program launches feel slower than they used to.
originalCommand: sc config SysMain start= disabled & sc stop SysMain
originalRevert: sc config SysMain start= auto & sc start SysMain

name: Disable Prefetch (SSD only)
description: Only for SSDs. Do NOT use on HDDs.
detailedDescription: The prefetcher records which files a program touches at startup and reads them in one pass next time. On a spinning disk that turns scattered seeks into a sequential read and helps a great deal, which is why the app refuses this on anything that is not a confirmed SSD.
originalCommand: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management\PrefetchParameters" /v EnablePrefetcher /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management\PrefetchParameters" /v EnablePrefetcher /t REG_DWORD /d 3 /f

name: Disable Nagle's Algorithm
description: TcpAckFrequency/TCPNoDelay on every interface.
detailedDescription: TcpAckFrequency/TCPNoDelay on every interface.

operations.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces' | ForEach-Object { Set-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name TcpAckFrequency -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force; Set-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name TCPNoDelay -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force }"

originalCommand: powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces' | ForEach-Object { Set-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name TcpAckFrequency -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force; Set-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name TCPNoDelay -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force }"
originalRevert: powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces' | ForEach-Object { Remove-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name TcpAckFrequency -EA 0; Remove-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name TCPNoDelay -EA 0 }"

name: Disable Network Throttling
description: Lifts the 10ms multimedia network throttle. Removes the throttle that protects audio and video playback from network interrupt load; under heavy traffic playback can stutter.
detailedDescription: NetworkThrottlingIndex caps non-multimedia network packets at roughly ten thousand per second so that audio and video playback cannot be starved by network interrupts. Removing the cap lifts a ceiling most connections never reach anyway. Undo it if playback stutters during heavy transfers.

name: Free QoS Reserved Bandwidth
description: Removes the 20% reserved bandwidth limit.

name: TCP Auto-Tuning + RSS
description: Balanced low-latency TCP settings.
originalCommand: netsh int tcp set global autotuninglevel=normal & netsh int tcp set global rss=enabled
originalRevert: netsh int tcp set global autotuninglevel=normal & netsh int tcp set global rss=enabled

name: Disable ECN
description: Turns off Explicit Congestion Notification. Congestion is then signalled by dropped packets instead of a marker, which on a busy line can be the worse trade.
detailedDescription: Explicit Congestion Notification lets a router mark a packet as congested instead of dropping it, so TCP can slow down without a retransmission. Turning it off means congestion is signalled by loss again. Some older equipment handles ECN badly, which is the case this helps.
originalCommand: netsh int tcp set global ecncapability=disabled
originalRevert: netsh int tcp set global ecncapability=enabled

name: Disable Delivery Optimization
description: Stops Windows Update P2P using your bandwidth.

name: DNS to Cloudflare (1.1.1.1)
description: OPTIONAL: sets DNS on all active adapters.
detailedDescription: OPTIONAL: sets DNS on all active adapters.

name: Clean Temp Files
description: Deletes %TEMP% and C:\Windows\Temp.

name: Empty Recycle Bin
description: Empties the Windows Recycle Bin.
detailedDescription: Empties the Windows Recycle Bin.

name: Clear Prefetch
description: Removes cached prefetch files.

name: Flush DNS Cache
description: ipconfig /flushdns.

name: Disable Reserved Storage
description: Frees ~7 GB reserved for updates.
detailedDescription: Frees ~7 GB reserved for updates.

name: Disable Hibernate (free space)
description: Removes hiberfil.sys (= your RAM size in GB). Hibernation and Fast Startup stop working. The space comes back the moment you re-enable it.
detailedDescription: Turning hibernation off deletes hiberfil.sys, which Windows sizes at roughly your installed memory. Fast Startup depends on the same file, so it stops working too. Re-enabling hibernation recreates the file and the space goes again.

name: Disable Advertising ID
description: No personalized ad tracking.

name: Disable Activity History
description: Stops Windows Timeline / activity feed.

name: Disable Tailored Experiences
description: No suggestions based on diagnostic data.

name: Disable Web Search in Start
description: Removes Bing/web results from Start search.

name: Disable Consumer Features
description: Stops auto-installed suggested/bloat apps.

name: Disable Location Services
description: Turns off Windows location access.

name: Disable Telemetry (DiagTrack)
description: Stops and disables the telemetry service. Feedback Hub and some Store and Update diagnostics stop working. Company-managed PCs may switch it back on.
detailedDescription: The Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service collects diagnostic data and uploads it on a schedule. Disabling the service and setting the policy to zero stops both. Feedback Hub and some Store and Update diagnostics stop working, and a company-managed machine may switch it back on.
originalCommand: reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection" /v AllowTelemetry /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f & sc stop DiagTrack & sc config DiagTrack start= disabled
originalRevert: sc config DiagTrack start= auto & sc start DiagTrack

name: Disable PCIe Power Saving (ASPM)
description: Stops PCIe links dropping to low power (GPU/NIC latency). PCIe links stay at full power, so idle power draw and heat go up.
detailedDescription: Active State Power Management lets PCI Express links drop to a low-power state between transfers, and bringing a link back up takes microseconds that show up as latency on a GPU or network card. Disabling it keeps the links awake. The cost is idle power and heat.

name: Force Platform Tick
description: Uses the platform tick source (pairs with dynamic tick off).
detailedDescription: Uses the platform tick source (pairs with dynamic tick off).

name: Disable CPU Idle States
description: Lowest latency, keeps CPU awake. More heat/power - desktops only. The CPU never idles: markedly more heat and power, and fans that never spin down. Desktops only.
detailedDescription: Processor idle states are the C-states a core enters when it has nothing to do, and coming back from a deep one takes longer than a shallow one. Disabling them keeps every core fully awake at all times. This is the most expensive power tweak here in heat and watts, and it is for desktops only.
originalCommand: powercfg -setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_PROCESSOR IDLEDISABLE 1 & powercfg -setactive SCHEME_CURRENT
originalRevert: powercfg -setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_PROCESSOR IDLEDISABLE 0 & powercfg -setactive SCHEME_CURRENT

name: Clear Pagefile at Shutdown
description: Wipes the pagefile on shutdown (slower shutdown).
detailedDescription: Windows normally leaves the pagefile intact between sessions. Clearing it on shutdown overwrites it, so nothing that was paged out survives the reboot. Shutdown takes noticeably longer, in proportion to how large the pagefile is.
originalCommand: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v ClearPageFileAtShutdown /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v ClearPageFileAtShutdown /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

name: Disable TCP Timestamps
description: Slightly leaner packets. Timestamps help TCP judge round-trip time on long or fast links; without them throughput can drop there.
detailedDescription: RFC 1323 timestamps add twelve bytes to every TCP packet and let the stack measure round-trip time precisely and detect wrapped sequence numbers. Dropping them makes packets slightly leaner. On a long or very fast connection those measurements are what keeps throughput up.
originalCommand: netsh int tcp set global timestamps=disabled
originalRevert: netsh int tcp set global timestamps=enabled

name: Disable RSC (Receive Coalescing)
description: Lower latency at a tiny CPU cost.
detailedDescription: Receive Segment Coalescing merges arriving packets into larger ones before handing them to the stack, which saves CPU and adds a little delay. Turning it off delivers each packet as it lands. The gain is latency, the cost is a slightly higher CPU load on heavy downloads.
originalCommand: netsh int tcp set global rsc=disabled
originalRevert: netsh int tcp set global rsc=enabled

name: Disable TCP Window Heuristics
description: Keeps your TCP window tuning from being overridden. Windows can no longer adjust the receive window for unusual connections by itself.
detailedDescription: Window scaling heuristics let Windows override your receive-window setting when it decides the connection looks unusual. Disabling them makes the setting you chose stick. The other side is that Windows can no longer adapt on a link where it would have been right.
originalCommand: netsh int tcp set heuristics disabled
originalRevert: netsh int tcp set heuristics enabled

name: Lower TcpTimedWaitDelay
description: Frees closed ports faster (helps many connections). Closed ports are reused sooner, so on a flaky line a late packet from an old connection can land on a new one.
detailedDescription: After a TCP connection closes, the port stays reserved for a while so that late packets from the old connection cannot be delivered to a new one. Lowering that wait from the default frees ports sooner. On an unreliable line it is exactly the protection you just shortened.

name: Raise MaxUserPort
description: More outbound ports available. Costs a little memory for the larger connection table, and changes nothing unless you open thousands of connections.
detailedDescription: MaxUserPort sets how many outbound ports are available for simultaneous connections. Raising it to the maximum matters for a machine opening thousands at once, and changes nothing at all for anything else. It costs a little memory for the larger table.

name: Disable Taskbar Widgets
description: Removes the Widgets button (frees a background process).

name: Disable Window Animations
description: Snappier minimize/maximize.

name: Disable Taskbar Animations
description: Removes taskbar animation overhead.

name: Disable Sticky Keys Prompt
description: No accidental Shift x5 popup mid-game.

name: Clear Windows Update Cache
description: Frees space from old update downloads. Recently installed updates can no longer be uninstalled afterwards, and Windows re-downloads whatever it still needs.
detailedDescription: The SoftwareDistribution folder holds update packages Windows has downloaded, including the ones it keeps so that a bad update can be uninstalled. Clearing it frees that space and removes that option. Windows re-downloads whatever it still needs.
originalCommand: cmd /c "net stop wuauserv & del /q /f /s %SystemRoot%\SoftwareDistribution\Download\* & net start wuauserv"

name: Clear Thumbnail Cache
description: Deletes cached Explorer thumbnails.

name: Enable Dark Mode
description: Dark theme for apps and system.
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize" /v AppsUseLightTheme /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize" /v SystemUsesLightTheme /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize" /v AppsUseLightTheme /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f & reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize" /v SystemUsesLightTheme /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f

name: Disable Aero Shake
description: Stops minimizing windows when you shake one.

name: Show Seconds in Clock
description: Taskbar clock shows seconds.

name: Show Hidden Files
description: Show hidden files and folders in Explorer.

name: Disable Snap Assist Flyout
description: No popup suggestions when snapping windows.

name: Disable Recent Files Tracking
description: Stops tracking recently opened documents.

name: Disable AutoPlay
description: No AutoPlay prompts for drives/media.

name: Disable Startup Sound
description: No Windows boot chime.

name: Disable Error Reporting
description: Stops Windows Error Reporting popups/uploads.
originalCommand: reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting" /v Disabled /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting" /v Disabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

name: Enable Taskbar 'End Task'
description: Adds End Task to the taskbar right-click (Win11).

name: Verbose Boot Messages
description: Shows detailed status during boot/shutdown. Boot and shutdown show technical status text instead of the plain spinner, which looks alarming if you are not expecting it.
detailedDescription: Verbose status replaces the plain spinner during boot and shutdown with the name of whatever Windows is currently doing. It is genuinely useful when something hangs and you want to know where. It changes nothing about speed and looks alarming if you are not expecting it.

name: Disable Lock Screen
description: Skips the lock screen (straight to login). You lose the lock screen with its clock, notifications and background - straight to the password prompt.
detailedDescription: The lock screen is the picture with the clock that appears before the password prompt. Disabling it goes straight to the prompt, saving a keypress. You lose the notifications and the clock that were shown there.

name: Classic Right-Click Menu (Win11)
description: Restores the full context menu. Restart Explorer after. The Windows 11 menu is gone, including the app entries only it shows. Explorer has to be restarted.
detailedDescription: Windows 11 shows a short context menu with the old one behind a second click. Registering an empty handler for the new menu's class makes Explorer fall back to the full one. Entries that only the new menu shows are then gone, and Explorer has to be restarted.

name: No Auto-Reboot on Updates
description: Windows won't force a restart while you're logged in.

name: Disable Cortana
description: Turns off the Cortana assistant.

name: Disable Start Menu Suggestions
description: No suggested apps/ads in the Start menu.

name: Disable Windows Tips
description: Stops 'tips & suggestions' popups.

name: Disable Lock Screen Ads
description: No Spotlight ads/tips on the lock screen.
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager" /v RotatingLockScreenOverlayEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager" /v SubscribedContent-338387Enabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager" /v RotatingLockScreenOverlayEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f & reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager" /v SubscribedContent-338387Enabled /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f

name: Disable Settings Suggestions
description: No suggested content in the Settings app.
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager" /v SubscribedContent-338393Enabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager" /v SubscribedContent-353694Enabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager" /v SubscribedContent-353696Enabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

name: Disable Cloud Clipboard Sync
description: No clipboard syncing across devices.

name: Disable Clipboard History
description: Turns off Win+V clipboard history. Win+V stops working, and nothing is kept beyond the single item you copied last.
detailedDescription: Clipboard history keeps the last several things you copied and syncs them if you let it. Turning it off keeps only the single most recent item, in memory. Win+V stops opening anything.

name: Disable App Diagnostics
description: Blocks apps from reading diagnostic info about other apps.

name: Disable Feedback Requests
description: Stops Windows asking for feedback.
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Siuf\Rules" /v NumberOfSIUFInPeriod /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f & reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection" /v DoNotShowFeedbackNotifications /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
originalRevert: reg delete "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Siuf\Rules" /v NumberOfSIUFInPeriod /f & reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection" /v DoNotShowFeedbackNotifications /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

name: Disable Typing/Inking Collection
description: Stops Windows learning from your typing/handwriting.
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Personalization\Settings" /v AcceptedPrivacyPolicy /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization" /v RestrictImplicitTextCollection /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f & reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization" /v RestrictImplicitInkCollection /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization" /v RestrictImplicitTextCollection /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization" /v RestrictImplicitInkCollection /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

name: Disable Handwriting Sharing
description: Stops sharing handwriting error reports.

name: Disable CEIP
description: Customer Experience Improvement Program off.

name: Disable Telemetry Tasks
description: Disables the scheduled telemetry/appraiser tasks. Compatibility data stops being collected, so Windows may no longer warn you about a known-incompatible program before a feature update.
detailedDescription: The Compatibility Appraiser and the two Customer Experience tasks scan installed software and report what they find, on a schedule, whether or not the telemetry service is running. Disabling the tasks stops the scans themselves. Windows may then not warn you about a known-incompatible program before a feature update.
originalCommand: schtasks /Change /TN "\Microsoft\Windows\Application Experience\Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser" /Disable & schtasks /Change /TN "\Microsoft\Windows\Customer Experience Improvement Program\Consolidator" /Disable & schtasks /Change /TN "\Microsoft\Windows\Customer Experience Improvement Program\UsbCeip" /Disable
originalRevert: schtasks /Change /TN "\Microsoft\Windows\Application Experience\Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser" /Enable & schtasks /Change /TN "\Microsoft\Windows\Customer Experience Improvement Program\Consolidator" /Enable & schtasks /Change /TN "\Microsoft\Windows\Customer Experience Improvement Program\UsbCeip" /Enable

name: Disable Error Reporting Service
description: Stops the WerSvc service. Crash reports are no longer collected, and a few programs use that service for their own crash dialog.
detailedDescription: Windows Error Reporting collects crash dumps and uploads them to Microsoft. Disabling the service stops the collection. A few programs use it for their own crash dialogs, and those will simply not appear.
originalCommand: sc config WerSvc start= disabled & sc stop WerSvc

name: Disable Maps Broker
description: Stops the Downloaded Maps Manager service. Offline maps stop downloading and updating in the Maps app.
detailedDescription: The Downloaded Maps Manager keeps offline maps updated in the background for the Maps app. If you do not use offline maps it does nothing for you. Undo it if maps stop working offline.
originalCommand: sc config MapsBroker start= disabled & sc stop MapsBroker

name: Disable Remote Registry
description: Blocks remote registry access (more secure). Remote administration tools that reach the registry over the network stop working - almost never used at home.
detailedDescription: Remote Registry lets another machine on the network read and write this one's registry, which is a domain administration feature. On a home machine nothing uses it and it is one fewer thing listening. Undo it only if a management tool needs it.
originalCommand: sc config RemoteRegistry start= disabled & sc stop RemoteRegistry

name: Disable LLMNR
description: Turns off Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution. Local devices without a DNS entry may stop being reachable by name, which some printers and NAS boxes rely on.
detailedDescription: Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution is the fallback Windows uses to find a device by name when DNS has no answer, by shouting on the local network. It is also a well-known route for credential relay attacks. Undo it if a printer or NAS stops being reachable by name.

name: Set Default TTL 64
description: Standard TTL value for outgoing packets. This only restores the standard value; expect no measurable change in speed or latency.
detailedDescription: The default Time To Live is how many hops a packet may take before routers discard it. Windows already uses 128 and this sets 64, which is what most other systems use. It changes nothing measurable about speed or latency; it is a cosmetic difference in what your packets look like.

name: Disable Teredo
description: Turns off Teredo IPv6 tunneling. Xbox networking and party chat rely on Teredo, so multiplayer through the Xbox app can stop working.
detailedDescription: Teredo tunnels IPv6 through an IPv4 network so that peer-to-peer connections can be made without native IPv6. Xbox networking and party chat are the main things on a home machine that use it. Undo it if multiplayer through the Xbox app stops connecting.
originalCommand: netsh interface teredo set state disabled
originalRevert: netsh interface teredo set state default

name: Disable Network Data Usage (Ndu)
description: Disables the Ndu driver (can reduce a known RAM leak). Task Manager and Settings stop reporting per-app network usage.
detailedDescription: The Network Data Usage driver is what lets Task Manager and Settings show per-application network usage, and on some builds it grows its non-paged pool over time. Setting its start type to disabled stops both the leak and the reporting. Undo it if you miss the per-app figures.

name: Rebuild Icon Cache
description: Clears corrupted/blurry icon caches.

name: Clear Font Cache
description: Rebuilds the Windows font cache.
detailedDescription: The font cache is a rebuilt index of every installed font, and a corrupted one shows up as missing or garbled text in programs rather than as an error. Clearing it means stopping the FontCache service, deleting the files and starting it again; Windows rebuilds the index on demand. Nothing is lost - the fonts themselves are untouched.
originalCommand: cmd /c "net stop FontCache & del /q /f /s %WinDir%\ServiceProfiles\LocalService\AppData\Local\FontCache\* & net start FontCache"

name: Reset Store Cache
description: Runs wsreset to clear the Microsoft Store cache.

name: Clear Crash Dumps
description: Deletes crash dump and minidump files.

name: Clear Event Logs
description: Wipes all Windows event logs.
detailedDescription: Wipes all Windows event logs.

name: Apply Max FPS Power Plan
description: Creates & activates a custom 'SlideTweaks Max FPS' plan (beyond Ultimate). Undo: switch to Balanced.
detailedDescription: Creates & activates a custom 'SlideTweaks Max FPS' plan (beyond Ultimate). Undo: switch to Balanced.

originalCommand: powershell -NoProfile -Command "$g=(powercfg -duplicatescheme e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61 2>$null); if(-not $g){$g=powercfg -duplicatescheme 8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c}; $id=[regex]::Match([string]$g,'([0-9a-fA-F-]{36})').Value; if($id){powercfg -changename $id 'SlideTweaks Max FPS' 'Max performance - SlideTweaks'; $P='54533251-82be-4824-96c1-47b60b740d00'; foreach($s in @(@('bc5038f7-23e0-4960-96da-33abaf5935ec',100),@('893dee8e-2bef-41e0-89c6-b55d0929964c',100),@('0cc5b647-c1df-4637-891a-dec35c318583',100),@('ea062031-0e34-4ff1-9b6d-eb1059334028',100),@('be337238-0d82-4146-a960-4f3749d470c7',2),@('45bcc044-d885-43e2-8605-ee0ec6e96b59',100),@('36687f9e-e3a5-4dbf-b1dc-15eb381c6863',0),@('75b0ae3f-bce0-45a7-8c89-c9611c25e100',0))){powercfg -setacvalueindex $id $P $s[0] $s[1]; powercfg -setdcvalueindex $id $P $s[0] $s[1]}; powercfg -setacvalueindex $id 2a737441-1930-4402-8d77-b2bebba308a3 48e6b7a6-50f5-4782-a5d4-53bb8f07e226 0; powercfg -setacvalueindex $id 501a4d13-42af-4429-9fd1-a8218c268e20 ee12f906-d277-404b-b6da-e5fa1a576df5 0; powercfg -setactive $id}"

name: Fast Keyboard Repeat
description: No delay, max repeat rate (snappier typing/keys).
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Keyboard" /v KeyboardDelay /t REG_SZ /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Keyboard" /v KeyboardSpeed /t REG_SZ /d 31 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Keyboard" /v KeyboardDelay /t REG_SZ /d 1 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Keyboard" /v KeyboardSpeed /t REG_SZ /d 31 /f

name: Mouse Data Queue Size 20
description: Smaller input buffer = fresher mouse data. Reboot. A community tweak with no measured benefit: a very small buffer can in theory drop input under extreme load. Reboot required.
detailedDescription: The mouse class driver buffers input reports in a queue, and a smaller queue means the newest report waits behind fewer old ones. The default of 100 is far larger than anything a working system fills. No measurement has ever shown this to help, and a very small buffer can in principle drop input under extreme load.

name: Keyboard Data Queue Size 20
description: Smaller keyboard buffer for lower input delay. Reboot. Same caveat as the mouse buffer - unproven, and a very small buffer can drop input under extreme load. Reboot required.
detailedDescription: The same buffer, on the keyboard class driver. The reasoning and the caveat are identical to the mouse queue: the default is far larger than a working system needs, and there is no measurement showing that shrinking it changes anything you can feel.

name: Instant Hover Response
description: Tooltips/hover react immediately (400ms -> 10ms).

name: Disable Filter Keys Prompt

originalRevert: reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Accessibility\Keyboard Response" /v Flags /t REG_SZ /d 126 /f

description: Trails, beeps, snap-to-button & window tracking off.
originalCommand: reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v MouseTrails /t REG_SZ /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v Beep /t REG_SZ /d No /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v ExtendedSounds /t REG_SZ /d No /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v SnapToDefaultButton /t REG_SZ /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v ActiveWindowTracking /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
originalRevert: reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v MouseTrails /t REG_SZ /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v Beep /t REG_SZ /d No /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v ExtendedSounds /t REG_SZ /d No /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v SnapToDefaultButton /t REG_SZ /d 0 /f & reg add "HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse" /v ActiveWindowTracking /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

name: Default Sensitivity (6/11)
description: Resets Windows pointer speed to the raw 6/11 notch. Overwrites your own pointer speed, so a sensitivity you had deliberately tuned is reset.
detailedDescription: Windows pointer speed has eleven notches, and only the sixth applies no multiplier to the counts your mouse reports. Any other notch scales them, which can drop or duplicate movement. This resets you to that neutral notch, overwriting a sensitivity you may have tuned on purpose.

name: Instant Window Focus
description: ForegroundLockTimeout 0 - windows take focus instantly. Any program can then pull focus instantly, including out of a running game.
detailedDescription: ForegroundLockTimeout is how long Windows blocks a background program from stealing focus after you last interacted. Setting it to zero removes the block, so a window you open appears in front immediately. It also lets anything else take focus instantly, including out of a game.

name: Input Driver Thread Priority
description: mouclass/kbdclass ThreadPriority 31. Community tweak - unproven, but harmless. Reboot.
detailedDescription: This raises the scheduling priority of the mouse and keyboard class drivers so their interrupt work is serviced sooner. It is a community tweak with no published measurement behind it, and no plausible way to make things worse. Requires a restart.
originalCommand: reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\mouclass\Parameters" /v ThreadPriority /t REG_DWORD /d 31 /f & reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\kbdclass\Parameters" /v ThreadPriority /t REG_DWORD /d 31 /f
originalRevert: reg delete "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\mouclass\Parameters" /v ThreadPriority /f & reg delete "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\kbdclass\Parameters" /v ThreadPriority /f

name: USB Input Power Saving Off
description: Disables Enhanced Power Management on mouse/keyboard USB devices. Reboot.
detailedDescription: Disables Enhanced Power Management on mouse/keyboard USB devices. Reboot.

operations.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\USB' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Get-ChildItem -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $dp = Join-Path $_.PSPath 'Device Parameters'; if (Test-Path $dp) { $svc=(Get-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name Service -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Service; if ($svc -match 'HidUsb|kbdhid|mouhid') { Set-ItemProperty $dp -Name EnhancedPowerManagementEnabled -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force; Set-ItemProperty $dp -Name SelectiveSuspendEnabled -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } } }"

originalCommand: powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\USB' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Get-ChildItem -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $dp = Join-Path $_.PSPath 'Device Parameters'; if (Test-Path $dp) { $svc=(Get-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name Service -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Service; if ($svc -match 'HidUsb|kbdhid|mouhid') { Set-ItemProperty $dp -Name EnhancedPowerManagementEnabled -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force; Set-ItemProperty $dp -Name SelectiveSuspendEnabled -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } } }"

name: Reset Boot Timers to Default
description: Sets useplatformtick + disabledynamictick back to Windows defaults. Reboot required.

name: Enable MSI Mode (GPU)

detailedDescription: Message-Signaled Interrupts for your graphics card - can lower latency/stutter. Reboot required.

detailedDescription: Stops Windows compressing RAM (saves CPU). Best with 16 GB+.

name: Xbox Button Doesn't Open Game Bar

detailedDescription: Stops Windows putting game controllers into power saving. Reboot.

detailedDescription: Turns off Windows audio effects on all playback devices (cleaner, lower latency).

operations.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\MMDevices\Audio\Render' -EA SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $p=Join-Path $_.PSPath 'FxProperties'; if(-not (Test-Path $p)){ New-Item -Path $p -Force | Out-Null }; Set-ItemProperty $p -Name '{1da5d803-d492-4edd-8c23-e0c0ffee7f0e},5' -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force -EA SilentlyContinue }"

originalRevert: powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\MMDevices\Audio\Render' -EA SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $p=Join-Path $_.PSPath 'FxProperties'; if(Test-Path $p){ Set-ItemProperty $p -Name '{1da5d803-d492-4edd-8c23-e0c0ffee7f0e},5' -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force -EA SilentlyContinue } }"

name: Audio Thread Priority
description: Gives the audio engine higher scheduling priority (MMCSS Audio task). Audio outranks other work, which on a weak CPU can cost frames.
detailedDescription: The multimedia scheduler runs registered tasks at raised priority, and this raises the Audio task's further. On a machine where audio crackles under load it is the direct fix. On a CPU that is already the bottleneck, the time has to come from somewhere.
originalCommand: reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile\Tasks\Audio" /v Priority /t REG_DWORD /d 6 /f & reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile\Tasks\Audio" /v "Scheduling Category" /t REG_SZ /d High /f & reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile\Tasks\Audio" /v "SFIO Priority" /t REG_SZ /d High /f

detailedDescription: Gives OBS / Streamlabs high priority so recordings stop dropping frames.

name: Games Priority Profile (MMCSS)
description: Gives games top GPU/CPU scheduling priority. Pairs with System Responsiveness. Games outrank everything else, so recording, streaming and voice chat get whatever is left.
detailedDescription: The Games task is the multimedia scheduler's profile for anything registering itself as a game, and this gives it top CPU and GPU scheduling priority. It pairs with System Responsiveness: one frees the headroom, the other decides who gets it. Recording, streaming and voice chat get whatever is left.

operations.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Class\{4d36e968-e325-11ce-bfc1-08002be10318}' -EA SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.PSChildName -match '^[0-9]{4}$' } | ForEach-Object { $d=(Get-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name DriverDesc -EA SilentlyContinue).DriverDesc; if($d -match 'NVIDIA'){ Set-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name PerfLevelSrc -Value 0x2222 -Type DWord -Force -EA SilentlyContinue; Set-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name PowerMizerEnable -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force -EA SilentlyContinue; Set-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name PowerMizerLevel -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force -EA SilentlyContinue; Set-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name PowerMizerLevelAC -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force -EA SilentlyContinue } }"

name: Global Timer Resolution
description: Makes a game's high-resolution timer request apply system-wide again (pre-2004 behaviour). Reboot required. A system-wide high-resolution timer raises power draw and hurts standby on battery. Reboot required.
detailedDescription: Before Windows 10 version 2004, one program asking for a high-resolution timer raised it for the whole system; afterwards it applies only to that process. This restores the old behaviour, which matters if a game depends on another process timing accurately. A system-wide high-resolution timer raises power draw and hurts standby, and it needs a restart.
